The paper (§3.6) explicitly adds training examples with only the final item masked, describing this as fine-tuning-like supervision, but gives no numerical mixing proportion or separate fine-tuning schedule. Ordinary Cloze training masks a random fraction ρ; reported settings are 0.6/0.4/0.2/0.2 for Beauty/Steam/ML-1m/ML-20m. Equation (8) averages negative log-likelihood over masked targets within each sequence. §3.4 truncates to the latest N items; inference appends [MASK] and predicts from its representation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690)

The released generator creates D ordinary masked copies plus one last-item-only copy **per training window**, then shuffles them together. With default/script D=10, explicitly forced endpoint examples constitute 1/11 ≈9.09% of examples, versus 10/11 ordinary reconstruction; ordinary copies can also mask endpoints. Long training histories become overlapping windows, rather than exclusively their latest N items (ML-1m script: N=200, stride=100). Ordinary masking selects min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length×ρ))) positions. Despite inherited 80/10/10 comments, mask_prob=1.0 replaces every selected item with [MASK]. Endpoint copies replace only the window’s final item. [Generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [script](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh)

Implementation loss sums cross-entropies over all real masked targets across the minibatch, divided by their count plus 1e−5; padded targets have zero weight. Thus 9.09% of examples does not imply 9.09% of loss weight. Released evaluation truncates history **including the held-out target** to N tokens, then replaces that target with [MASK]—equivalent to latest N−1 observed items plus an appended mask. Endpoint supervision is therefore established prior practice; any proposed weighting needs comparison against this existing construction. [Loss](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py), [evaluation construction](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py)
